name: India-based data engineer investigating European relocation

constraints: Needs explicitly stated employer sponsorship and relocation support
Will not infer eligibility from employer reputation
context.company_awareness: Most employers unknown; starting with roles and destination countries

trigger: A professional contact relocates to Europe, prompting the engineer to test whether comparable roles explicitly support international applicants before investing in applications.

searches_run.query: data engineer jobs Germany Netherlands visa sponsorship relocation
searches_run.observation: Results included sponsor-focused aggregators, employer postings and role mismatches. Some aggregators equated recognised-employer status with sponsorship-labelled roles; these claims were not verified or adopted as eligibility evidence.

searches_run.query: data engineer Amsterdam Berlin relocation support no visa sponsorship job
searches_run.observation: Results surfaced explicit negative sponsorship language, including a Berlin ATS posting. The opened HSO role describes support limited to the Netherlands alongside European residence/work-rights wording; this requires clarification for an India-based applicant.

sources.title: Data Engineer jobs in the Netherlands — Konijn Jobs
sources.supports: Retrieved aggregator page markets sponsorship using recognised employer status. Recorded only as competitor positioning; no legal thresholds, role-level sponsorship or counts are accepted as verified.

sources.title: HSO International - Data Engineer
sources.supports: Direct employer inspection shows Netherlands-limited sponsorship/relocation wording, a European work-rights statement, English fluency and Microsoft data-stack requirements. It does not clearly establish that this India-based persona can be hired.

sources.title: Data Engineer — Clera
sources.supports: Retrieved ATS snippet states Berlin on-site work and that visa sponsorship is unavailable. Not independently opened.

best_entry_page.primary_query: data engineer jobs Europe relocation support
best_entry_page.promise: Find relevant data roles and inspect the employer's published sponsorship and relocation statements, separating explicit support, exclusions and unknowns.
best_entry_page.cta: Search by destination and stack, then save alerts after checking the source requirements.
proof_needed: Demonstrate role-level source text rather than a company-wide sponsor badge.
Keep sponsorship and moving-cost support as separate criteria.
Clarify contradictory or conditional text without treating it as approval.
Verify employer coverage and data-stack filtering.
Show how Pro description checks preserve unknowns; they are not immigration or employer verification.
Create a new indexable guide with carefully limited claims.

conversion_objections: Will sponsorship results actually include people applying from India?
Are employer-wide badges being confused with this vacancy?
Can I see the exact sentence before spending time applying?
Will I discover employers before being asked to choose them?
Does relocation mean payment, administrative help or merely permission to move?

avoid_targeting.reason: Neither hiring nor legal approval can be guaranteed.
Immigration calculations are not this product's demonstrated capability.

avoid_targeting.query: all recognised sponsors hiring data engineers
avoid_targeting.reason: Registered company status does not establish current role-level support.

message_to_founder: Simulation: I do not have a European employer shortlist yet. Help me find technically relevant roles and show exactly what each employer says about sponsorship and moving, including the cases where the answer is unclear.
confidence_and_limits: Synthetic scenario, not immigration advice. Two queries and one employer inspection reveal ambiguous support wording and strong aggregator promises; they establish neither legal eligibility nor hiring probability. Exact stack and citizenship are not supplied; no personal eligibility conclusion is made.
